# Library Setup
```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tinytex)
```

\newpage
# Question 1 (a)

```{r Q1a, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Q1.a

# Load the dataset
propertydataset <- read.csv("PropertyDataset1.csv")

# Check the first few rows of sale_date to confirm its format
head(propertydataset$sale_date)

# Convert sale_date to Date type (assuming the format is DD/MM/YYYY)
propertydataset$sale_date <- dmy(propertydataset$sale_date)

# Check if the conversion worked by printing the first few rows of the sale_date column
head(propertydataset$sale_date)

# Check for NA values in sale_date after conversion
sum(is.na(propertydataset$sale_date))

#Change to numeric
propertydataset$num_bedrooms <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", propertydataset$num_bedrooms))
propertydataset$num_bathrooms <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", propertydataset$num_bathrooms))

# Filter for houses sold in 2017 with 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms
house_2017 <- propertydataset %>%
  filter(year(sale_date) == 2017, num_bedrooms == 3, num_bathrooms == 2)

# View the filtered data
head(house_2017)
```
\newpage
# Question 1 (b)

```{r Q1b, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Q1.b

# Extract numeric property size from the description and create a new numeric column
propertydataset <- propertydataset %>%
  mutate(
    property_size_numeric = as.numeric(str_extract(property_size_description, "\\d+"))
  )

# Filter data for premises sold in Cork or Galway and greater than 125 square metres
cork_galway_data <- propertydataset %>%
  filter(
    county %in% c("Cork", "Galway"),  # Filter for Cork or Galway
    property_size_numeric == 125      # Area greater than 125 square metres
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(price))                # Order by price from highest to lowest

# View the filtered and sorted data
head(cork_galway_data)
```

# Question 1 (c)

```{r Q1c, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Q1.c

# Filter for new dwelling houses or apartments in the specified areas
new_dwelling_house_apt <- propertydataset %>%
  filter(
    county == "Dublin",                       # Ensure the county is Dublin
    grepl("Dublin 18|Dublin 16|Dublin 15|Dublin 8|Dublin 4", post_code),
    grepl("New Dwelling house|New Apartment", property_description)                
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE),  # Calculate the average price
    max_price = max(price, na.rm = TRUE),  # Calculate the maximum price
    min_price = min(price, na.rm = TRUE)   # Calculate the minimum price
  )

# View the resulting summary data frame
print(new_dwelling_house_apt)
```

# Question 1 (d)

```{r Q1d, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Q1.d

# View unique values in the property_description column
unique(propertydataset$property_description)

# View the frequency of each value in the property_description column
table(propertydataset$property_description)

# View unique values in the property_description column
unique(propertydataset$county)

# View the frequency of each value in the property_description column
table(propertydataset$county)

# Standardize all variations of "second-hand dwelling house/apartment" to 
"second-hand dwelling house/apartment"
propertydataset$property_description <- gsub(
  pattern = "second-hand dwelling house / 
  apartment|second-hand dwelling house /
  Apartment|Second-Hand Dwelling house /
  Apartment|second-hand dwelling house /Apartment", 
  replacement = "second-hand dwelling house/apartment", 
  x = propertydataset$property_description, 
  ignore.case = TRUE
)


# Check the first few rows to ensure the replacement worked
head(propertydataset$property_description)

# Check to ensure the changes have been applied correctly
head(propertydataset$property_description)

# Create a named vector for standardizing county names
county_map <- c(
  "Leitrim" = "Leitrim", 
  "Dublin" = "Dublin", 
  "Kilkenny" = "Kilkenny", 
  "Kildare" = "Kildare", 
  "Tipperary" = "Tipperary", 
  "Louth" = "Louth", 
  "Limerick" = "Limerick", 
  "Cork" = "Cork", 
  "Clare" = "Clare", 
  "Wexford" = "Wexford", 
  "Roscommon" = "Roscommon", 
  "Kerry" = "Kerry", 
  "Waterford" = "Waterford", 
  "Sligo" = "Sligo", 
  "Westmeath" = "Westmeath", 
  "Wicklow" = "Wicklow", 
  "Donegal" = "Donegal", 
  "Offaly" = "Offaly", 
  "Mayo" = "Mayo", 
  "Meath" = "Meath", 
  "Carlow" = "Carlow", 
  "Longford" = "Longford", 
  "Cavan" = "Cavan", 
  "Laois" = "Laois", 
  "Galway" = "Galway", 
  "Monaghan" = "Monaghan", 
  "westmeath" = "Westmeath", 
  "dublin" = "Dublin", 
  "Corcaigh" = "Cork", 
  "Dubln" = "Dublin", 
  "cork" = "Cork", 
  "Ros Comain" = "Roscommon", 
  "wicklow" = "Wicklow", 
  "kildare" = "Kildare", 
  "Tipp " = "Tipperary", 
  "limerick" = "Limerick", 
  "donegal" = "Donegal"
)

# Use recode to standardize county names
propertydataset$county <- recode(propertydataset$county, !!!county_map)

# Check the first few rows to ensure the replacement worked
head(propertydataset$county)

# Create a bar chart showing the number of properties sold in different counties
# Color the bars based on property type (e.g., house or apartment)
ggplot(propertydataset, aes(x = county, fill = property_description)) +
  geom_bar() +  # Use a bar chart
  labs(
    title = "Properties Sold by County in Ireland",
    x = "County",
    y = "Number of Properties Sold",
    fill = "Property Type"  # Label for the legend
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +  # Use a minimal theme
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)
    )# Rotate x-axis labels for readability
```

# Question 1 (e)

```{r Q1e, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Q1.e

# Filter the dataset for sales between 2015 and 2017
sales_2015_2017 <- propertydataset %>%
  filter(year(sale_date) >= 2015 & year(sale_date) <= 2017)

# Create a bar plot showing the number of different types of houses sold by year
ggplot(sales_2015_2017, aes(x = factor(year(sale_date)), fill = property_description)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack") +  # Stack bars for each property type
  labs(
    title = "Number of Different Types of Houses Sold (2015-2017)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Houses Sold",
    fill = "Property Type"  # Legend label
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +  # Minimal theme for better aesthetics
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)  # Rotate x-axis labels for readability
  )
```

# Question 1 (f)

```{r Q1f, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Q1.f


# Remove columns from "num_bedrooms" to "not_full_market_price"
propertydataset <- propertydataset %>%
  select(-num_bedrooms, 
         -num_bathrooms, 
         -property_size_description, 
         -property_description, 
         -not_full_market_price)

# Filter rows for Dublin, Cork, Galway, and Semidetached house, then arrange by price
semidetach <- propertydataset %>%
  filter(county %in% c("Dublin", "Cork", "Galway"), 
         formatted_description == "Semi-Detached House") %>%
  arrange(price)

# View the first few rows of the filtered and arranged data
head(semidetach)
```

# Question 1 (g)

```{r Q1g, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Q1.g

# Filter houses greater than €200,000 from Galway, Roscommon, Mayo, or Sligo
houses_more_than_200000 <- propertydataset %>% 
  filter(county %in% c("Galway", "Roscommon", "Mayo", "Sligo"),
         price > 200000) %>% 
  mutate(year = year(sale_date)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(year))  # Remove rows with missing years

# Summarize by year and county to handle multiple entries per year
houses_summary <- houses_more_than_200000 %>% 
  group_by(year, county) %>%
  summarise(avg_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE))

# Create a line graph with ggplot
ggplot(houses_summary, aes(x = year, y = avg_price, color = county, group = county)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Price Trends of Houses Greater than €200,000",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Price (€)",
    color = "County"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Galway" = "blue", "Roscommon" = "green",
    "Mayo" = "red", "Sligo" = "purple"
  )) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

```
